candidates.summary: cmd/gnoweb's default -trusted-paths and -index-community=registered lend a stranger's h1 and paragraph to <title> and description on staging.gno.land, whose chain never enables r/sys/names
candidates.failure_scenario: misc/loop/docker-compose.yml runs ghcr.io/gnolang/gno/gnoweb:master for staging.gno.land with neither -trusted-paths nor -index-community, against the portal loop chain, whose genesis (gno.land/genesis/genesis_txs.jsonl via misc/loop/scripts/start.sh) never calls r/sys/names.Enable. With verifier.gno's `enabled = false`, any account (funded by faucet-api.staging.gno.land) can addpkg under any namespace; addpkg_namespace.txtar shows `gno.land/r/randomname/one` answering OK before Enable. A stranger deploys gno.land/r/gnoland/airdrop rendering `# Official GNOT airdrop` plus a lure paragraph. gnoweb classifies it official and serves title `Official GNOT airdrop - gno.land`, the lure as description, robots `index, follow`, followed internal links and no realm notice. On master the same page was titled `gno.land - /r/gnoland/airdrop` with an empty description, so the lending comes from this PR. The ADR's own rule, that a chain without r/sys/names runs -index-community=none and its trusted list means nothing, is not applied to the in-tree staging deployment, which the PR leaves unchanged.
candidates.verify_by: cp tests/b1-lines-removed-claims-reach-catalog-loop-defaults_test.go gno.land/cmd/gnoweb/zz_loop_defaults_test.go && go test ./gno.land/cmd/gnoweb -run TestLoopDefaultsLendUnenforcedNamespace -v -count=1; then the read-only probe `gnokey query vm/qeval --data "gno.land/r/sys/names.IsEnabled()" -remote https://rpc.staging.gno.land:443`, expect `false bool` (staging RPC answered 503 this session, so the live state is inferred from the genesis files)

candidates.summary: gnodev staging keeps DefaultTrustedPaths and -index-community=registered on a chain that never enables r/sys/names, and gnodev has no flag to change either
candidates.failure_scenario: `gnodev staging`, which docs/resources/gnodev.md describes as tuned for server use, boots a chain where r/sys/names stays `enabled = false`: nothing in contribs/gnodev calls names.Enable. Any account can therefore deploy under `gnoland` or any other name, including the preloaded devtest account. gnoWebAppConfig leaves staging on gnoweb's default list and on `registered`. A deployer's gno.land/r/gnoland/airdrop is official: its h1 and paragraph become <title> and description with `index, follow`. Any other name, such as /r/brandname/airdrop, counts as registered and is indexed. The ADR says such a chain should run -index-community=none and treat its trusted list as meaningless, but gnodev exposes neither -trusted-paths nor -index-community, so a staging operator cannot follow that advice.
candidates.verify_by: cp tests/b1-lines-removed-claims-reach-catalog-staging-trust_test.go contribs/gnodev/zz_staging_trust_test.go && cd contribs/gnodev && go test . -run TestStagingTrustsNamespacesItsChainDoesNotEnforce -v -count=1; grep -rn 'sys/names\|Enable' contribs/gnodev/pkg/dev (expect no Enable call)

candidates.summary: RenderRealm walks the document for md.Lead on every render, though community pages, the user view and the README view discard it
candidates.failure_scenario: handler_http.go:903 (user page) and :1063 (README) call RenderRealm as `_, err :=`. For every community page, mayRepeat is false, so the lead is never used. Each of these renders still pays the Lead walk and its buffers. The author's own benchmark after the 16-byte writer is 27 MB per op on a 20k-emphasis lead, which a community realm can force on every view for a value nobody reads.
